name: example-generic-round
description: Round-duct fittings only. Every zeta here is a typical textbook-order value chosen to exercise the format; none is measured vendor data. Replace with vendor data before sizing real work. Sizes are the duct diameter in mm: size_min_mm/size_max_mm = [d].

fittings.source: typical value, smooth 90 deg round elbow R/D = 0.75, example entry - replace with vendor data
typical value, smooth 90 deg round elbow R/D = 1.0, example entry - replace with vendor data
typical value, smooth 90 deg round elbow R/D = 1.5, example entry - replace with vendor data
typical value, smooth 90 deg round elbow R/D = 2.0, example entry - replace with vendor data
fittings.notes: Listed after the tighter radii on purpose: with identical windows, Match() by type returns the first entry (R/D 0.75). Use ById() to pick a specific radius, or give each radius its own type.

fittings.source: typical value, 90 deg round tee, branch leg referred to branch velocity, example entry - replace with vendor data
typical value, 90 deg round tee, straight-through leg referred to main velocity, example entry - replace with vendor data
fittings.notes: Distinct type so it does not shadow the branch leg under first-match-wins. 'tee_straight' has no built-in correlation fallback.

fittings.source: FittingsLibrary.ReducerRound at d_out/d_in = 0.8, 45 deg (0.04 + 0.37*(1 - 0.64) = 0.1732), referred to outlet velocity; example entry - replace with vendor data
fittings.notes: 'reducer' has no built-in correlation fallback in ZetaFor(); a catalog entry is the only way to supply it.

fittings.source: FittingsLibrary.DamperButterfly(100) = 0.10 fully open; example entry - replace with vendor data
